newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan floods wreck houses, at least 4,000 stranded.
newsitem.headline: Sudan floods wreck houses, at least 4,000 stranded.

text.p: Floods have destroyed more than 2,600 houses in Sudan's Khartoum province, a Sudanese newspaper reported on Friday.
The privately-owned Akhbar al-Youm daily said floods swept away 2,618 houses in the southern Jebel Aulia area where at least 4,000 people were stranded without a shelter.
Twenty-eight schools were also damaged but there were no casualties, it said.
Torrential rains have lashed Khartoum for the past two weeks, killing at least 15 people in the northern Geili area.
Early on Friday, Sudanese state television warned residents of the capital's southern suburbs of Al-Saha and Zebra that floods from the neighbouring Gezira state were approaching.
It showed residents and civil defence forces setting up sandbanks and draining off the water.
Khartoum's northern areas were saved from flooding on Wednesday after the water naturally changed its path and drained in the Nile, Sudanese newspapers said.
